questions.q: Smoke particles in air are seen to move randomly under a microscope. What causes this motion?
options: the smoke particles repelling each other
light from the microscope heating the particles
questions.why: Brownian motion: tiny, fast, randomly moving air molecules hit the larger smoke particles unevenly.

questions.q: A sealed gas cylinder of fixed volume is heated. Why does the gas pressure increase?
options: the particles move faster and hit the walls more often and harder
there are more particles in the cylinder
the particles expand and push on the walls
questions.why: Higher temperature means faster particles, so more frequent and harder collisions give more force per unit area.

questions.q: Which surface is the best emitter of thermal radiation?
questions.why: Dull black surfaces are the best emitters (and absorbers) of infrared radiation.

questions.q: State two differences between evaporation and boiling.
questions.model: Evaporation happens at any temperature, boiling only at the boiling point; evaporation happens only at the surface, boiling happens throughout the liquid (bubbles form).
points: evaporation at any temperature / boiling at a fixed temperature (boiling point)
evaporation only at the surface / boiling throughout the liquid
